newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil up on refinery hitches, diesel short.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil up on refinery hitches, diesel short.

text.p: NWE gas oil firmed considerably on Monday and traders expected more gains after two big refineries in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam area ran into difficulties, dealers said.
IPE Oct climbed just $1.75 to $247.50 a tonne, but November narrowed the gap with October, jumping $5.25 to $240.75.

The unexpected closure of a gas oil pipeline at Shell's Pernis refinery forced the company to buy 40,000 tonnes of barges, traders said. And a wildcat strike at BP/Texaco's Pernis plant also ate into distillate production, a union leader said.
"That just threw petrol onto the flames," a trader added.
Heating oil barge premiums jumped by $1.50 to a high of $8.50 over Oct futures, and several companies ended the day with unsatisfied demand for diesel.
A diesel cargo arriving on Nov 3-7 in Hamburg was sold at Nov IPE +$22 cif on Monday, but dealers saw premiums rising to $30 in the next few days.

Algerian exports, previously confined to the Mediterranean market, were expected to sail north. A large proportion of the 570,000 tonnes U.S. gas oil fixed to sail to Europe last week were expected to be sold into the Oct IPE contract.
